standard_prerequisites.statement: Wolpert's twist formula: the rate of change of L(c) with respect to the twist parameter around c* equals the sum of the cosines of the angles of intersection of c with c*

core_obligations: Open with the C-generic case: the lemma follows from Wolpert's twist formula and Proposition Thurstonprop (proof line 402).

Construct the arc set A for the non-generic case: choose the multicurve m = c*, find the arcs e1 and e2 with sign changes of the intersection cosines on either side of c*, and build central arcs whose geodesic representatives are disjoint from c, using the normal-neighbourhood cycles A_i and the ccstar figure (proof lines 404-421).

Close via the Lipschitz map: gluing strips for the central arcs turns c* into a piecewise geodesic shortened by shifting (the newfig figure), and the 1-parameter family of maps with strips wider at central arcs gives a derivation strictly negative on L(c) and strictly positive on every c' in C without c (proof lines 423-432).

Construct the arc set A: arcs e1 and e2 from sign changes of intersection cosines on either side of c*, central arcs from the normal-neighbourhood cycles, homotopically nontrivial by minimal intersection of c*.

Close with Thurston's Lipschitz map: central-arc strips shorten the shifted piecewise geodesic, and the width choice gives the derivation strictly negative on L(c) and strictly positive on C without c.

statement_spans.label: author Proposition environment, source label balancedlem (statement, source lines 577-580)

proof_spans.label: the author's own proof environment immediately following it (source lines 581-596)

standard_prerequisites.name: Corollary 3.10 (source label linear)
standard_prerequisites.statement: unique minimum point p(C,d) of the restricted lengths on each E(C,d); supplies the point through which the level-set foliation argument runs

standard_prerequisites.name: Lemma 2.5 (source label lemma14)
standard_prerequisites.statement: empty boundary of Min(C); combined with Foote's classical theorem to conclude L(t) is C^1

core_obligations: Set up the Lagrange-multiplier characterization: at x not in Min(C), balancedness at x is equivalent to a normalised positive k-tuple a with v_C equal to the weighted sum of gradients (proof line 582).

Prove the Claim: for x in E(C,d) minus Min(C), v_C equals the convex combination with the parameters of the point p(C,d) in Min(C) (proof lines 584-595): define the level sets L(t), use Theorem 10 of SchmutzMorse (C^1 submanifold), Foote's classical result (boundary of a tubular neighbourhood is C^1) and lemma14 (empty boundary), then Lagrange multipliers along transverse paths.

Conclude by letting t vary: the tuple d(x) is the parameter value of the minimum of the weighted length function, and v_C is parallel to the weighted gradient everywhere on E(C,d(x)) (proof line 595).
proof_roadmap: Reduce balancedness to a Lagrange-multiplier normalisation.

State and prove the Claim via the level sets L(t) (boundaries of tubular neighbourhoods of the C^1 cell Min(C)), invoking SchmutzMorse Theorem 10, Foote's classical smoothness result and lemma14 for empty boundary; transversality of E(C,d(x)) against L(t) gives normality of the weighted gradient.
Vary t to identify the weights with the tuple d(x) and conclude parallelism everywhere.
metadata.difficulty_reason: Lagrange-multiplier argument layered on the differential structure of Min(C): tubular neighbourhoods, C^1 regularity of level-set boundaries via Foote, transversality, and a parameter-identification step closing the Claim.

statement_spans.label: author Proposition environment, source label balancedlemnonfilling (statement, source lines 598-601)

proof_spans.label: the author's own proof environment immediately following it (source lines 608-628)

standard_prerequisites.name: Lemma 3.5 (source label polyhedronargument)
standard_prerequisites.statement: gradient linear independence for minimal filling sets away from minima; underlies embeddedness of the loci E(C',d)

standard_prerequisites.name: Lemma 3.9 (source label minimalem)
standard_prerequisites.statement: minima of C' occur only within Min(C); underlies the foliation of Teichmuller space by the loci with varying d

standard_prerequisites.name: Proposition 2.2 (source label Thurstonprop)
standard_prerequisites.statement: Min(C') empty in Teichmuller space for nonfilling C'; forces the completion-boundary analysis

standard_prerequisites.name: Lemma 2.5 (source label lemma14)
standard_prerequisites.statement: structure of Min(C) used in the boundary analysis

core_obligations: Case C' a subset of a minimal filling set: the loci E(C',d) are embedded submanifolds foliating the space with varying d, from polyhedronargument and minimalem (proof line 609).

Case C' a multicurve: minima live on the noded-surface boundary strata of the Weil-Petersson completion; invoke the wolpert2005 distance expansion (the paper's corollary wolcor, lines 613-620, delivered verbatim inside the proof) and conclude balancedness for multicurves (proof lines 611-623).

core_obligations: Set up the inequality (ineq, equation at proof lines 697-700) and the locus C_ineq on which it holds; the projected gradients look like those at a point of Min(c(f)) (proof lines 694-703).

Establish the three without-loss-of-generality assumptions: linear independence of the outside gradients (via neededtofill discards), linear independence and convex-hull membership for v_{c(f)} on C_ineq, and strict inequality at x (via Wolpert convexity); the tipover figure illustrates why linear independence cannot break down where v_{c(f)} is nonzero (proof lines 705-724).

Prove the Claim (strict inequality propagates over the component E'(C,d(x))) by contradiction with a Lagrange-multiplier argument on the flow-box level sets L(y,t), analogous to balancedlem with Conv(C) in place of Min(C); the q1 figure shows the locus configuration (proof lines 726-755).

Close by following the path gamma of minima towards the Weil-Petersson boundary: d takes only regular values (Remark holdsonnbhd, lines 759-762, delivered verbatim inside the proof), the collar lemma blocks monotone decrease at the pinched multicurve, and the |C without c(f)|>1 case reduces via the averaged length function (proof lines 764-772).
proof_roadmap: Set up the inequality and the locus C_ineq; the projected gradients look like those at Min(c(f)).

Make the three assumptions without loss of generality: discard dependent curves via neededtofill, keep v_{c(f)} independent and in the convex hull, upgrade equality to strict inequality via Wolpert's convexity.
Prove the propagation Claim by contradiction with Lagrange multipliers on flow-box level sets, in analogy with balancedlem using Conv(C).

Follow the minima path gamma to the completion boundary: regular values of d, the collar lemma at the pinched multicurve, and the averaged-length reduction for more outside curves give the contradiction.
metadata.difficulty_reason: Ninety-line proof: three without-loss-of-generality reductions, a propagation Claim with a flow-box plus Lagrange-multiplier argument, a path-of-minima limit to the Weil-Petersson boundary blocked by the collar lemma, and a generalisation step for multiple outside curves.

core_obligations: Define L(C,t,d), the sublevel intersection D(C,t,d), and the H-property: three face conditions (unique face per subset C', connected unit tangent cone, codimension |C'|-1) at proof lines 448-461.
Prove the Claim that C-generic points satisfy the H-property, via twist-path product structures and the R-factors of the twist flow (proof lines 466-471).

Drop genericity: full tangent cone from Thurstonprop when C does not fill and from defnmod when C fills; H-property implies linear independence (the explicit R^4 example f_1..f_4 shows the converse fails); transfer off the C-generic set using LipschitzMap, Thurstonprop and measure zero of nongeneric points (proof lines 473-483).
proof_roadmap: Case split as in LipschitzMap.
Define D(C,t,d) and the H-property with its three labelled-face conditions.
Establish the C-generic Claim through twist paths and R-factors.

Then remove genericity: nonfilling case via Thurstonprop's full cone, filling case via defnmod; separate H-property from linear independence with the explicit R^4 example; conclude by the measure-zero transfer of the failure set away from minima.
